title: LLM landing: sandbox compatibility certification and smoke runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a reproducible, low-friction certification and smoke-runbook that validates new open-source LLM weights through intake -> conversion -> runtime compatibility -> pin recommendation -> profile publish. This ticket scopes the smoke checklist, test harness automation, and the operator runbook used by model validators. The goal is to reduce manual gating time by 60% and catch common incompatibilities before models reach the staging catalog.

Background: We onboard community weights in a variety of formats (Torch state_dict, safetensors, gguf, ONNX). Past issues include mismatched layer names, dtype/quantization mismatches, KV cache shape errors at runtime, and memory blow-ups during conversion. Current intake flow runs ad-hoc tests which are unevenly applied by engineers.\n
Scope: 1) A deterministic smoke suite (small sample inference across runtimes: native runtime, ONNX path, and CPU fallback) validating correctness and basic perf metrics; 2) A documented runbook for model validators that includes triage steps and links to automated conversions (safetensors -> runtime format -> quantized variants); 3) Automated pass/fail thresholds for publishing a profile (latency p50/p95, tokenization checksum, top-k sample similarity delta, KV cache warmup behavior); 4) CI jobs and a Grafana smoke dashboard.

Non-goals: Full evaluation harness (ML perf/regression suites) and customer-facing perf benchmarks. This ticket is for the fast gating checks only.
acceptance_criteria: A smoke suite exists that runs a deterministic 16-token generation across three runtimes and reports p50/p95 latencies
Conversion artifacts (canonical runtime tarball) are produced and linked to a sample PR on github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-converters
Operator runbook with triage steps for five common failure modes is published in Confluence and referenced from the intake UI
Model profile publish is blocked if any smoke check fails; we can toggle gating in the staging environment
A Grafana dashboard shows latest smoke run results per model with pass/fail badges
steps: Design smoke inputs: seed, prompt set (2-3 prompts), tokenizer checksum harness
Implement converter wrapper: unify safetensors/torch/gguf -> runtime format with deterministic ops
Wire the converted artifact into a lightweight staging runtime (1-GPU micro-pool) for smoke runs
Collect metrics: p50/p95 token latency, peak memory, token-accuracy proxy (nll/perplexity delta vs baseline), kv-cache-check (shape + warmup iterations)
Add gating logic to intake orchestrator: publish-profile if all checks green, otherwise fail with failure-reason tags
Publish runbook in Confluence with recovery commands, common fix snippets, and escalation contacts
Add CI job that runs suite on PR to runtime-converters and intake orchestration repo
Create Grafana panel and add alert to SRE for repeated failures (>3 consecutive on same model family)
